newsitem.title: USA: Albanians could disrupt Serb control - NY Times.
newsitem.headline: Albanians could disrupt Serb control - NY Times.

text.p: American intelligence officials believe an ethnic Albanian group has the potential to disrupt Serb control of its province of Kosovo, the New York Times reported on Sunday.
The Kosovo Liberation Army is a shadowy group about which little information is known, but it has staged at least five armed attacks in the last year, the Times reported.

The Times interviewed the leader of the group on the condition he remain anonymous, but identified him as "one of the most wanted terrorists in Yugoslavia." The Times reported that the interview was the first contact the rebel group had with Western media.

"We are not a terrorist organisation," the man, who called himself "Alban," told the Times. "We have the support of nearly all Albanians. The only attacks we carry out are against the representatives of the Serbian regime."
About 90 percent of Kosovo residents -- 2.2 million people -- are ethnic Albanians, the Times said. The Kosovo Liberation Army also receives support from 700,000 Albanians living abroad.
Alban predicted Serbian authority in Kosovo would crumble within three years.

The armed resistance started with the 1995 Bosnia peace agreement, the Times said. Until then, ethnic Albanians had withdrawn from political life in Kosovo after Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic annulled Kosovo's bid to become an independent nation. The region was part of Albania until after the First World War.
Kosovo is a mostly Albanian province in Serbia
